written.q: Define cloud computing and list the five essential characteristics defined by NIST. (6 marks)
written.a: Cloud computing is the delivery of computing as a service rather than a product, where shared resources, software and information are provided to devices as a metered service over a network (on-demand IT on a pay-as-you-go basis). NIST characteristics: on-demand self-service (provision without human interaction), broad network access (standard devices over the network), resource pooling (multi-tenant shared resources), rapid elasticity (scale out and in quickly), measured service (usage monitored and billed).

written.q: Compare IaaS, PaaS and SaaS in terms of what the customer manages, with one example each. (6)
written.a: IaaS: provider manages networking, storage, servers and virtualization; the customer manages the OS, middleware, runtime, data and applications (AWS EC2). PaaS: the provider also manages OS, middleware and runtime; the customer manages only the application and data (Google App Engine). SaaS: the provider manages the whole stack; the customer only uses the software (Gmail, Microsoft 365).

written.q: Distinguish public, private and hybrid clouds and state one advantage of each. (6)
written.a: Public: owned by a third party and shared over the Internet — low cost and high scalability. Private: operated exclusively for one organization — high security, control and compliance. Hybrid: public and private bound together with data/app portability — flexibility and cost optimisation (keep sensitive data private, burst peaks to public).

written.q: Explain the shared responsibility model with an example. (4)
written.a: Security is split: the provider is responsible for security OF the cloud (physical infrastructure, network hardware, hypervisor); the customer is responsible for security IN the cloud (data encryption, IAM, network configuration, application security). E.g. if a customer misconfigures an S3 bucket as public and data leaks, it is the customer's responsibility.

written.q: "Serverless means there are no servers." Discuss. Give two advantages and two disadvantages of serverless computing. (5)
written.a: False: servers still exist, but the provider provisions, scales and manages them, so developers do not. Advantages: no server management; auto-scales to zero and pay only per invocation (also fast deployment). Disadvantages: cold-start latency; harder debugging.

written.q: Differentiate between a virtual machine and a container. (4)
written.a: A VM virtualizes the hardware and runs a full guest OS on a hypervisor — strong isolation, but GBs in size and minutes to boot. A container packages the app and dependencies and shares the host OS kernel through a container runtime — lighter (MBs), starts in seconds, more portable, weaker isolation.

written.q: Compare edge, fog and cloud computing. Why does an autonomous vehicle need edge computing? (6)
written.a: Cloud: centralized data centres, high latency (50–150 ms), massive compute, batch analytics. Fog: between edge and cloud, medium latency (10–50 ms), aggregates edge data. Edge: on device/gateway, ultra-low latency (<10 ms), lightweight real-time compute at the source. A vehicle must brake within milliseconds; waiting for a round-trip to a far data centre is too slow and the connection may drop, so decisions are made at the edge.

written.q: State three principles of Zero Trust security. (3)
written.a: Verify explicitly (authenticate using identity, location, device health, workload); least privilege (minimum access only when needed); assume breach (design as if attackers are inside, minimise blast radius, segment access).

written.q: Explain why virtualization is called the core enabler of cloud computing. (4)
written.a: A hypervisor divides one physical server into many isolated VMs. This allows resource pooling and multi-tenancy (many customers on shared hardware), high utilisation (server consolidation), rapid provisioning (on-demand self-service, elasticity), and snapshotting/migration for resilience — all the properties the cloud depends on.

written.q: Give four FinOps techniques for reducing cloud costs. (4)
written.a: Right-sizing instances; reserved instances for predictable workloads (up to 72% saving); spot/preemptible VMs for fault-tolerant work (60–90% discount); auto-scaling down when idle; storage tiering; cost-allocation tags.

written.q: Why do 87% of enterprises use a multi-cloud strategy? (5)
written.a: To avoid vendor lock-in; to use best-of-breed services from each provider; for regulatory compliance (in-country providers); for cost arbitrage between providers; and for redundancy (fail over during one provider's outage).

written.q: Explain the 5 V's of big data. (5)
written.a: Volume (amount: 120+ ZB in 2024), Velocity (speed of arrival, real-time streams), Variety (structured, semi-structured, unstructured), Veracity (quality and accuracy), Value (insights and business decisions).
